correctness.rationale: For each pattern, applying a letter map sums the exact occurrence counts of its preimages since admissible position tuples are independent of the labels. A disagreement survives a map assigning its two symbols distinct labels. If a third symbol is present, preserve it as a third label; that would give a genuinely three-symbol ternary collision. The independently reproduced census excludes this and establishes the stated exact binary pairs and binary injectivity for lengths 3 through 12. At length 13 the exhaustive run finds 8188 distinct binary decks among 8192 words and 1594311 distinct ternary decks among 1594323 words. The only nonsingletons are four and twelve doubletons, respectively, and the ternary pairs are exactly the unordered two-letter embeddings of the binary pairs. Replay with Python 3 and NumPy using evidence/1/owned_deck_census.py; the exact class output is evidence/1/full_census.txt. The reproduction decodes all words by base-q digits, enumerates each allowed tuple and groups full fixed-width byte keys, not hashes; each count fits in one byte since it is bounded by max(13,66,165), and every repeated fiber was required to have size two. The frozen C++ and supplementary Python code were inspected, not executed. The four binary pairs are closed under swapping labels, and every endpoint uses both symbols, so arbitrary-q collisions form a matching with four disjoint edges per support pair. Choosing all isolated vertices and one endpoint per edge proves both codebook formulas. The lower lengths follow by binary projection at a disagreement. Literal length 2 is degenerate (01 and 10 collide), excluded explicitly by the frozen Finding.
